chapter: Road bands: Hampton, Crawford and Mingus
title: Lonnie Hillyer and the Mingus band's comic repertoire at Monterey
summary: He assesses Hillyer and recalls the group playing 'Cocktails for Two' and marching off to 'The Saints' after being cut off at Monterey.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene

blocks.x: He was a very fine trumpet player out of Dizzy Gillespie. He’s traditional. He didn’t have the chop and the strength that Dizzy had, you know, but he played that kind of stuff on the instrument. He was a good trumpet player.
And he and Charles McPherson together…
Yeah, well that was Mingus’ group and they had a very, very good group.

They played a lot of great music as well as a lot of funny music. They “Cocktails for Two” and Mingus would have us play that with the whole band sometimes, “Cocktails for Two.” “When The Saints Go Marching In,” we played. When we couldn’t play all of the music that we had together at Monterey, they kicked us off after…I don’t know, 25 minutes or something. Mingus was pissed so he had us play “When The Saints Go Marching In” and we marched around the stage, and marched off the stage and he cursed out Jimmy Lyons of the Monterey Jazz Festival. The things that don’t get spoken about many times are the interesting things that musicians go through. That’s why oral history is very, very important, you know?
